courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Chemolingot Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC Chemolingot Campus is in Tiaty, Baringo County. It admitted its first students in 2021 and was officially opened on 2 August 2024, and it holds 69 students. It is a SECOND KMTC campus in Baringo County, distinct from KMTC Kabarnet which is listed separately here - both were checked against sources naming each campus by name before either was recorded, because two campuses of one college in the same county defeat every county-level check. This is the only programme the campus currently runs; the Ministry of Health has been directed to introduce more, and planned programmes are not recorded here. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for its certificate programmes. Certificate courses run two years, except Enrolled Community Health Nursing which runs two and a half. KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). The total here is that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only - accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm the current structure and the intake months with the campus before applying.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Kabarnet Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

Bomet University is public and CUE-chartered - the 36th, chartered on 4 February 2026, having operated as Bomet University College since Legal Notice 145 of 2017. It publishes 76 academic programmes of which 18 are undergraduate. THIS RECORD CLOSES A BLOCKER THIS CATALOGUE HAD NAMED: Bomet was listed with two programmes because a general search returned only two, and the note said its own listing was the last thing to be indexed. The programmes are published on the SCHOOL sites - sbe.buc.ac.ke for business and economics, soe.buc.ac.ke for education - which is the same lesson Borabu and Alupe already taught here: search the institution's own domain, and when it is large, its school's. Entry is the national KUCCPS degree minimum of C+ with subject requirements per programme; the education degrees ask for a C+ in each of the two teaching subjects. No per-programme price exists to quote: Kenya retired the Differentiated Unit Cost in May 2023 for the Student-Centred Funding Model, under which what a student pays is set by an assessed means band, so the fee could not be verified as a course total. See the funding note on this card for what you would be asked for.

courses.course_name: Diploma in Clinical Medicine and Surgery
courses.institution: Tenwek Hospital College of Health Sciences
courses.verification_note: Tenwek Hospital College of Health Sciences trains inside Tenwek Mission Hospital in Bomet County, under the Africa Gospel Church with World Gospel Mission, and has trained nurses there since June 1987. It publishes its own size - 130 to 150 students at any one time - and two independently phrased searches name the same two entry-level diplomas and nothing else. ENTRY IS MORE OPEN HERE THAN AT KMTC: a C plain mean grade, with a C plain in English or Kiswahili, a C plain in Biology and a C- in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or Physical Science, plus an entrance examination and an interview. KMTC asks C+ for the same award, so a learner holding a C plain who has been told these courses are closed to them may still have a route here. DURATION IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT. The college names a September intake and publishes no length, and no length for this award at this institution is reachable from here. This catalogue records 36 months for the same award elsewhere because those institutions publish it; transferring that figure would assert an institution fact nothing sourced supports. Ask the college how long the programme runs. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: no fee figure of any kind was returned by any reachable source - a found absence rather than a refused reading. The fee could not be verified; ring the college.

That is a found absence rather than a reading Njia refused, so nobody re-runs the search expecting a number. The fee could not be verified; ring the college.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Busia Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Garissa Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

Certificate courses run two years, except nursing which runs two and a half. KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Total here is that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only - accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying.

Entry grade and structure from KUCCPS and TSC: the P1 certificate has been phased out and the Diploma in Primary Teacher Education is now the minimum qualification TSC will register, entered on a KCSE mean grade of C plain over three years at one of 33 public teacher training colleges, with placement through KUCCPS and assessment by KNEC. Fee derived from the Ksh 67,189 first-year figure published for KUCCPS-placed students at public TTCs - the same government consolidated rate used across public TVET - scaled to three years; one college separately quotes about Ksh 205,000 for the full course inclusive of admission, practicum and KNEC assessment, which agrees within two per cent. Outcome figures are null rather than estimated: with roughly 369,000 registered teachers unemployed, any employment rate Njia invented here would be actively misleading. Confirm fees with the college.

courses.verification_note: Manna Bible Institute and School of Missions is an interdenominational Bible college at Ongata Rongai, teaching since 1986 and registered by TVETA as a technical and vocational college. The award is named on the institute's own course listing and repeated by a second, differently phrased search. Entry is recorded as OPEN: the institute publishes no KCSE requirement and describes itself as open to anyone seeking Bible-based training. Ask what it expects of an applicant with no KCSE certificate. No programme length is published anywhere reachable, so the duration is empty rather than guessed, and the institute does not publish a fee for this course. Classes start the first Monday of every month, with distance and online routes alongside the residential one. ALSO NAMED AND NOT RECORDED: a Certificate and Diploma in Biblical Counselling, named by one listing and not repeated by the second; and a BA in Practical Ministry, described as starting rather than running.

Umma University is CUE-chartered and KUCCPS-approved, and is the first Islamic chartered university in Kenya (cross-reported August 2026). It is a private university and sets its own fees; its fee schedule could not be verified from any source reachable here, so no figure is shown rather than a guessed one. Confirm the fee, the current entry requirement and which campus runs the programme before you plan around it. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: one search gave Ksh 56,000 per trimester across the board and the next gave Ksh 49,000 for Business and Ksh 17,500 for Islamic Sharia - a threefold spread between programmes, and the two readings disagree on Business. None of these is this course’s fee - treat it as a bracket to check, and ask which AWARD the quote covers and what it excludes.

Umma University is private and CUE-chartered, grown out of the Thika College of Sharia and Islamic Studies, with campuses at Thika and Kajiado, learning centres at Garissa and Mombasa and a TVET institute at Thika Makongeni. Its five schools are Business and Technology, Education, Islamic Studies and Arabic, Nursing and Health Sciences, and the computer science department within Business and Technology. Listed on the university's own academics and school listings. Entry is the national C+ degree minimum; nursing carries cluster-subject requirements above it. UPGRADING NURSING IS NOT RECORDED - it is for people already registered and practising, and this catalogue is read by people deciding what to do after KCSE. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: one search gives Ksh 56,000 a trimester across the university, the next gives Ksh 49,000 for business and Ksh 17,500 for Islamic Sharia - a three-fold spread between programmes, and the two readings disagree on business. Umma prices per programme rather than per institution, so no single figure is attributable here. The fee could not be verified, so none is shown; ask which figure applies to this named award and per what period.

courses.course_name: Diploma in Clinical Medicine and Surgery
courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Kakamega Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Total here is that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was recorded here as a C+ mean grade and that was wrong in the exclusionary direction. The Clinical Officers Council bar, standard at every accredited college teaching this diploma and carried by the fourteen other KMTC records of the same award in this catalogue, is a mean grade of C plain, with a C plain in Biology and in English or Kiswahili and a C- in Chemistry and in Mathematics or Physics. A grade quoted high removes the card from the reader who needed it.

courses.institution: Masinde Muliro University of Science and Technology (MMUST)
courses.verification_note: MMUST is public, CUE-chartered, in Kakamega, and runs over 400 programmes across eleven schools - and this catalogue held two of them. Listed on the university's own school structure, which two independently phrased searches name the same way: Agriculture and Veterinary Sciences, Public Health, Biomedical Sciences and Technology, Engineering and the Built Environment, Business and Economics, Computing and Informatics, Education and Social Sciences, Science, Nursing, and Disaster Management and Humanitarian Assistance. Entry is recorded at the national KUCCPS degree minimum of C+, the door rather than the queue; MMUST publishes subject requirements per programme - good mathematics and physics grades for engineering, and the health programmes are competitive. Duration is the standard national programme length for each award, five years for engineering and four for the rest, which is a qualification-level fact rather than a figure read off this university's calendar. The university does not publish a per-programme price for this course.

courses.course_name: Artisan in Fashion Design and Clothing Technology
courses.verification_note: Programme named in Sigalagala National Polytechnic's published artisan course list, with a stated minimum of D- for this course. The institution's published artisan minimum is given as KCPE or KCSE mean grade D-. A KCPE certificate is an alternative to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it, so a learner holding an E clears the published bar and E is recorded. That is the same reading already applied at Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti, whose published minimum has the identical shape. Recording the D- branch instead removed this course from the screen of the learner least likely to have another option, and left Kakamega reading as blind to an E-grade learner while this polytechnic sat in the catalogue. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026). Ask the registrar whether KCPE alone is accepted.

Kenya Highlands University is a CUE-chartered evangelical Christian private university at Kericho, founded in 1989, and had not been listed here at all. Programme named in the university's published undergraduate list. Entry follows the national university minimum of a KCSE C+ together with the subject requirements for the chosen major. One thing this record cannot express in a grade: the university states that applicants are expected to show a personal commitment to an evangelically interpreted Christian life and demonstrable service or leadership in a church or Christian organisation. That is a real condition of admission, it is not academic, and no KCSE result substitutes for it - weigh it before applying. Which regime you are in changes the answer more than which course you pick. None of these is this course’s fee - treat it as a bracket to check, and ask which AWARD the quote covers and what it excludes.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Kapkatet Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.course_name: Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN)
courses.institution: AIC Kijabe College of Health Sciences
courses.verification_note: AIC Kijabe College of Health Sciences trains inside Kijabe Mission Hospital at Lari in Kiambu County, run by the Africa Inland Church, and its nursing programme is accredited by the Nursing Council of Kenya. This is the first mission-hospital training school in this catalogue: a whole category of faith-based provision that serves exactly the reader Njia is built for and had never been listed. Both the college and this programme are named by two independently phrased searches. ENTRY IS MORE OPEN HERE THAN AT KMTC AND THAT IS THE POINT OF LISTING IT. The published bar is a C plain mean grade, with a C plain in English or Kiswahili, a C plain in Biology or Biological Sciences and a C- in Mathematics, Physics or Chemistry. KMTC asks C+ for the same award, so a learner holding a C plain who has been told nursing is closed to them may still have a route here. Confirm the current requirement with the college before applying. DURATION IS SOURCED AND IT IS THREE AND A HALF YEARS, not the three this catalogue records for KRCHN elsewhere. The college publishes 3 years 6 months, which is what 42 months here means, and it matches what several KMTC campus listings say about the same award. Njia records 36 months across the rest of the estate and that discrepancy is unresolved rather than settled by this record - it is flagged here because this is the first record in the catalogue carrying the longer figure from its own source. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: the college is reported at Ksh 56,000 per semester, payable in instalments. No total is written from it, because the number of semesters in a three-and-a-half-year programme is not published anywhere reachable and multiplying by a semester count I picked myself would be inventing the part that matters. The fee could not be verified as a course total, so none is shown - but the per-semester figure is here because a reader ringing the college is better off knowing the order of magnitude than being told nothing. Intake months are NOT recorded as sourced: one search gives March and October, the other January and September. Two sources disagreeing about a date is the one thing this catalogue treats as more perishable than a fee, so the card keeps its standing caveat to confirm with the institution. Also not recorded: a three-year Kenya Registered Clinical Medicine and Surgery diploma appears in one listing only, and the college’s higher diplomas in critical care nursing, nurse anaesthesia and perioperative nursing are post-basic routes for people already registered and practising.

courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). This campus opens for its pioneer intake in September 2026 with roughly 1,000 places, applications through the KUCCPS student portal at students.kuccps.ac.ke closing 23 August 2026. courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Kisii Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. Maseno University is public and CUE-chartered, near Kisumu, running fourteen schools that span medicine, law, pharmacy, nursing, planning and architecture, agriculture, computing and the sciences. Listed on the university's own bachelors programme listing and that school structure, named the same way by two independently phrased searches. THE AWARD NAMES CARRY MASENO'S OWN "(with IT)" CONVENTION, which the university appends across its undergraduate programmes; a reader searching the exact title is who that matters for. Entry is the national KUCCPS degree minimum of C+ except where this record says otherwise, and it is the door rather than the queue - confirm the programme code and the current cut-off on the KUCCPS student portal for your cycle. The Council of Legal Education also sets subject requirements for law entry, typically a B plain in English or Kiswahili; confirm the current cluster before applying. An aggregator quotes Ksh 70,000 to 150,000 a year across all Maseno programmes; that is neither published by the university nor attributable to a named course, and it sits outside the SCFM mechanism entirely, so it is named here only so nobody mistakes it for a price. Programme named as an artisan course in Kinango Technical and Vocational College's published 2025/2026 course list, cross-reported by Business Radar (June 2025) and Education News Hub, September 2026. Duration of one year is published for the programme. ENTRY IS RECORDED AS OPEN, AND THE SOURCES CONFLICT: one states a KCSE minimum of D-, while the college's own artisan requirement is given as "a KCPE certificate or equivalent". A KCPE certificate is an ALTERNATIVE to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it - KCPE is not marked in letter grades at all - so a learner holding an E clears the published bar. That is the same either/or already resolved this way at Sigalagala, Siaya, Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti. Quoting the stricter figure would remove the card from the screen of the reader with the fewest options, who could then not even ring up to ask. Confirm with the college before travelling. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (inclusive of assessment fees, effective May 2026), scaled to the twelve-month duration. Kinango TVC is a public institution and that national rate applies; it bills per term and additional mandatory charges are reported separately (hostel Ksh 4,000 per term, library Ksh 900, student activity Ksh 1,000 a year). Confirm with the registrar.

courses.verification_note: Entry requirement is a KCSE mean grade of C- with C- in Biology or Biological Sciences, per the Kenya Veterinary Board's published minimum entry requirements for animal health courses and the institute's own listing. courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts in Communication and Public Relations
courses.verification_note: This course previously displayed a precise-looking tuition figure that was never observed anywhere. An audit found the same value repeated across unrelated institutions - Ksh 420,000 appeared on twelve different degrees at twelve different universities, public and private, from nursing to design to actuarial science - which is not what real fee data looks like. It was a placeholder, so it has been removed rather than left wearing a caveat. The figure could not be verified against any source reachable here, so nothing is shown. Ask the institution directly; if it is a public university, note that a single per-programme price no longer exists. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: fees here are charged per credit hour with 129 credit hours required to graduate. Two readings of the same 2025/26 document gave Ksh 5,650/6,410 and Ksh 6,640/7,380 for the Athi River and Nairobi campuses - a 15% disagreement, which across 129 credit hours is a difference of well over Ksh 100,000. None of these is this course’s fee - treat it as a bracket to check, and ask which AWARD the quote covers and what it excludes.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Machakos Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Machakos Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Total here is that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Named on this campus's own list, not inferred from KMTC's national one. KMTC Machakos opened in 1959 as a training school for Enrolled Nurses under the then Machakos General Hospital, replaced that award with Kenya Enrolled Community Health Nursing in 1978 and with the KRCHN diploma in 2000, and holds about 900 students beside Machakos County Teaching and Referral Hospital, its clinical site. A programme list carrying dates like that is the strongest attribution available for a KMTC campus, because a national template cannot fake them. This is the ONE programme two independently phrased searches both name here, and neither query contained it. Four other programmes appear in one listing only and are therefore not recorded: a Certificate in Medical Engineering in the first, and Orthopaedic and Trauma Medicine, Occupational Therapy and Clinical Medicine and Surgery in the second. One of them may well run here - ring the campus rather than reading their absence as evidence. Higher Diploma in Critical Care Nursing is excluded on a different ground: it is post-basic, for people already in practice. One source gives the diploma entry bar as a C- mean grade. That is NOT what is recorded: KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C plain for its diploma programmes, corroborated across several campus listings, and the eligibility rule here forbids quoting a grade high but has never licensed quoting one low - a learner sent at a diploma on a C- they cannot use is harmed in the other direction. C plain is recorded, the conflict is stated, and the campus is the place to confirm it.

courses.institution: Methodist College of Health Sciences, Maua
courses.verification_note: Methodist College of Health Sciences sits inside Maua Methodist Hospital at Maua in Igembe South, Meru County, under the Methodist Church in Kenya. The hospital opened in 1928 and is a 230-bed referral hospital serving about 600,000 people in Meru North; training began there in 1942 and the college is Nursing Council of Kenya accredited. ENTRY IS MORE OPEN HERE THAN AT KMTC: a KCSE mean grade of C plain, with a C plain in English and Kiswahili and a C- in Physics, Mathematics or Chemistry. KMTC asks C+ for the same award. The grade was not put into the query that returned it, so it is not an echo of the question. Confirm with the college before applying. Mombasa County holds TWO distinct KMTC campuses and this catalogue recorded them as one until now. This is the older of the two: founded in 1948 at Lady Grigg maternity to train enrolled nurses and midwives, moved to Tononoka in Mombasa Island in 1980, beside Coast General Hospital, and holding about 1,200 students. Its other programmes are NOT recorded, and the reason is worth stating rather than hiding: one listing names Medical Laboratory Sciences, Health Records and Information Technology, Orthopaedic Technology and Medical Imaging Sciences at this campus, and a second, independently phrased search named only Clinical Medicine and Surgery and Medical Laboratory Sciences. Only the programme both agree on is recorded. Ring the campus about the rest rather than assuming they are absent. Entry is the Clinical Officers Council bar applied at every accredited college: a C plain mean grade, with a C plain in Biology and in English or Kiswahili and a C- in Chemistry and in Mathematics or Physics.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Murang'a Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.institution: Institute for Meteorological Training and Research (IMTR)
courses.verification_note: IMTR is the training branch of the Kenya Meteorological Department at Dagoretti Corner and a World Meteorological Organization Regional Training Centre for English-speaking Africa. ENTRY IS RECORDED AS OPEN BECAUSE THE INSTITUTE ASKS FOR A CERTIFICATE RATHER THAN A GRADE: it states an O-Level certificate, and a certificate is an alternative to a mean grade rather than a bar set above one, so a learner holding a KCSE at any grade clears what is published. courses.course_name: Bachelor of Arts in Biblical Studies
courses.verification_note: KAG EAST University is a CUE-chartered private university owned by the Kenya Assemblies of God church, formerly the East Africa School of Theology. It was named on this catalogue’s own known-missing list of chartered private universities and is now listed. Programme named by two independently phrased searches; neither query contained the programme names. The county needs stating plainly because the sources contradict each other. Both describe a campus at Buru Buru in NAIROBI - one gives a street address, next to Mutindwa Market on Mumias South Road, Phase 4 - and both also describe a Kitengela site in KAJIADO, one calling it the current main campus and the other a 58-acre property being developed into one. Nairobi is recorded because it is the campus both sources place precisely; Kitengela is a genuine second site and a lead for a separate row, not evidence that this one is in the wrong county. The university also runs an extension campus in Kisumu and cohorts in Malindi, Mombasa and Kitale, none of which are listed. Entry is recorded at the C+ mean grade the university publishes as its KCSE minimum, which matches the CUE and KUCCPS national degree bar; it also admits on a KNEC or KASNEB diploma or an equivalent from a CUE-recognised examining body. No fee is shown. Searching returned no figure of any kind for this university, so it could not be verified and nothing is written rather than a guess. Ring admissions for the current schedule and ask what it excludes. Eight further degrees appear in one listing only and are therefore not recorded - Education, Business Administration, Criminology and Security Management, Early Childhood Development, Church Educational Ministries, Counselling Psychology, Journalism and Mass Communication, and Community Development - as do a Bachelor of Arts in Religious Education and a Bachelor of Arts in Bible and Theology in the other. Any of them may well run; ring the university rather than reading their absence here as evidence.

This is a KASNEB national professional qualification, examined by the Kenya Accountants and Secretaries National Examinations Board rather than awarded by the college. KCA University teaches it through its School of Professional Programmes, which runs satellite centres in Nairobi CBD, Githunguri, Kericho, Eldoret, Kisumu, Amagoro and Kitengela - the teaching is what is attributed to KCA here, and the award is KASNEB's. The entry bar is KASNEB's own published requirement rather than the university's. KASNEB publishes the ATD bar as a KCSE mean grade of C-, which is the point of it: it is the recognised route into accountancy for a learner below the C+ the professional qualifications ask, and passing it is itself an accepted entry qualification for CPA. NO DURATION IS RECORDED and that is a property of the qualification rather than a gap: KASNEB examinations are sat level by level at the candidate's own pace, so how long it takes depends on how many sittings are passed and when. Kenya Airways Pride Centre is the airline's own training academy at Embakasi, KCAA-approved for aviation security and accredited by IATA and ICAO — the first training facility in Africa to earn IATA's dangerous-goods excellence certification. Published tuition runs from about Ksh 170,000 to Ksh 300,000 depending on programme, with a non-refundable application fee of Ksh 2,000; the centre does not publish a per-course fee in any source reachable from here, so no figure is shown rather than the midpoint of that range - Ksh 235,000 appears in no source and was displayed identically on a 12-month diploma and a 6-month certificate. Cabin crew roles also carry airline-set physical requirements — published minimum heights are 5.4 feet for women and 5.6 feet for men — which no grade will substitute for. Confirm the fee and the requirements with the centre.

KASNEB publishes the qualification and the Kenya School of Law its own intakes, so award and delivery are sourced separately. Entry is a C+ KCSE aggregate, or two KACE principal passes with credits in Maths and English at KCE level, or an existing KASNEB technician, diploma or professional certificate — that last route is the one to look at if your KCSE mean fell short. THE INTAKE MONTHS HERE ARE SOURCED, WHICH ALMOST NO RECORD IN THIS CATALOGUE CAN SAY: the School of Law runs January, May and September intakes deliberately aligned to KASNEB’s April, August and December sittings. The qualification runs over three levels — Foundation at six units, Intermediate at five and Advanced at four. You must register with KASNEB before enrolling for classes. KASNEB registration and examination fees are paid to the board and not to the college, so tuition is not the whole cost; and no fixed length is published, because levels are sat at the candidate’s own pace. The School publishes no fee for this course in any source reachable from this build.

The Kenya School of Law is a state corporation established under the Kenya School of Law Act, and this is the one programme it runs that a school leaver can enter directly - placement is through KUCCPS, which opened the May 2026 intake in February 2026. Published entry is a KCSE mean grade of C plain with at least a C+ in English or Kiswahili, so the subject grade is the real gate and a C plain alone is not enough. Alternative routes are published too: one principal pass at KACE, a pass in a certificate of law course at an accredited legal education provider, or a certificate of experiential learning from the Council of Legal Education. Two academic years minimum, three maximum. Teaching runs at the Karen campus and the Nairobi Town campus on Moi Avenue, weekday in-person days with virtual evening classes. Njia does not list the Advocates Training Programme, which is the school's better-known course: it is postgraduate and requires a law degree, so it is not a route from KCSE and listing it here would mislead. The school sets its own fees and does not publish a figure for this programme in any source reachable from this build, so it could not be verified and no figure is shown rather than a guessed one - ring the school for the current schedule.

The Railway Training Institute is a public TVET institution under the Ministry of Transport, with campuses at South B in Nairobi and a marine school at Kisumu. CORRECTING AN EARLIER NOTE HERE, which said RTI publishes no fee schedule: it publishes a TERM-BASED one. Two independently phrased searches corroborate the term counts - a CBET Level 6 diploma runs NINE TERMS full-time at a KCSE C- (engineering also asking passes in Mathematics, Physics and English), a Level 5 certificate SIX TERMS at a D plain - and the hostel at Ksh 19,500 a term with meals, or Ksh 5,000 a term for day-scholar lunch. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: per-term figures of about Ksh 36,600 for diploma Module 1 and Ksh 36,100 or 32,100 for Modules 2 and 3, certificates about Ksh 33,600 and 33,100 - but the same source also gives the diploma Term 1 as Ksh 38,600, the figure it separately gives for a HIGHER diploma. A source contradicting itself inside one paragraph attributes nothing, and a Term 1 figure usually carries one-off charges, so multiplying by nine would overstate it. The fee could not be verified, so no total is written. THE DURATION IS GONE RATHER THAN REPLACED BY A GUESS: this record said 24 months, which no source supports. RTI publishes a term COUNT, and converting nine terms to months needs the terms in its academic year, which is not published anywhere reachable. Ask the institute how many terms it runs a year and what the whole programme costs.

ALSO NAMED ON THE SAME ADVERTISEMENT AND NOT RECORDED: a Higher Diploma in Civil Engineering Construction with Building and Civil Engineering, Building Economics and Structures options — that is a post-diploma progression award rather than an entry route from school — and a Certificate in Building Technology, which runs but whose KCSE mean grade is not published in any source reachable from this build, so recording it at open entry would quote a grade low. The award, the C- diploma bar and the January, March and September intakes are published by the institute itself, and the programme list is corroborated by its own September 2026 intake advertisement. IT IS EXAMINED BY KNEC AND RUNS IN THREE MODULES (I, II and III): Module I is the entry point from KCSE and the later modules are progression within the same award, so this is one record rather than three. NO LENGTH IS RECORDED: RTI publishes a term count (three terms per module) and the number of terms in its academic year is not published anywhere reachable, so it is not converted. RTI publishes no fee for this course that Njia could reach; a non-refundable application fee of Ksh 1,000 is charged. Ring +254 740 859 121.

Strathmore publishes the entry routes on its own professional-courses and ACCA pages. THE BAR IS A C+ KCSE MEAN WITH A C IN BOTH ENGLISH AND MATHEMATICS — the subject requirement is a C, not the C+ that CPA asks beside it. SECOND PATHWAYS MATTER MORE THAN THE BAR IF YOU MISSED IT: two A-level principal passes, an ABE certificate, CPA Part 1, the Accounting Technician Course at intermediate or final level, a degree, or ACCA’s Foundation in Accounting certificate all admit you without the C+. KASNEB registration and examination fees are paid to the board and not to the college, so tuition is not the whole cost; and no fixed length is published, because levels are sat at the candidate’s own pace. Strathmore prices per programme and publishes no fee for this course that Njia could reach, so none is shown; ask whether a quoted figure covers one level or the whole qualification.

Programme total published by Strathmore Law School: Ksh 2,051,438 for the four-year, eight-semester LLB, confirmed against two independent reports of the same schedule (about Ksh 250,000-258,000 a semester) and stated to cover lectures, course materials, a laptop and an academic trip abroad. fee_observed is NOT set: this is read from reporting of the schedule rather than off the university own current fee structure, so the record stays derived rather than published. ENTRY IS THE PUBLISHED BAR, NOT THE EXCEPTION: the school states an aggregate KCSE B with a B in English or Kiswahili, and that a B- may exceptionally be considered - B is recorded, because the exception is discretionary and recording B- would quote the bar low. A grade alone does not secure a place: every candidate meeting the requirement sits a University entrance examination in English (Ksh 2,000) and an oral interview, and this is reported as the most selective LLB entry in the country. The July intake is the published single intake for this programme, which is why it is stated here rather than left to the catalogue default cycle.

Strathmore publishes the entry routes on its own Certified Public Accountants page. THE BAR IS A C+ KCSE MEAN WITH A C+ IN BOTH ENGLISH AND MATHEMATICS — a step above the C that ACCA asks at the same institution, so do not read one bar off the other. Alternative routes: two KACE principal passes with credits in Maths and English at KCE level, the Kenya Accounting Technicians Certificate, the Accounts Clerk National Certificate, or a degree. KASNEB registration and examination fees are paid to the board and not to the college, so tuition is not the whole cost; and no fixed length is published, because levels are sat at the candidate’s own pace. Strathmore prices per programme and publishes no fee for this course that Njia could reach, so none is shown.

Duration is the standard Kenyan programme length for the award - four years for a Bachelor of Technology and five for a Bachelor of Engineering - which is a qualification-level fact rather than a figure read off this university's own calendar. The university does not publish a per-programme price for this course.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Nakuru Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Kapsabet Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. Dedan Kimathi University of Technology is public and CUE-chartered, on the main Nyeri campus 160km north of Nairobi, and this catalogue held two of its programmes. courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

courses.verification_note: Kenya School of Agriculture is a college under the State Department for Crops Development, TVETA-licensed and KNEC-examined, main campus at Wambugu farm in Nyeri. Entry is a D plain for craft certificates, C- for diplomas. DURATION REMOVED RATHER THAN GUESSED: this said 12 months, which nothing supports. The school gives its programmes as three years overall, this catalogue records the craft certificate as TWO MODULES, and no reachable source says how long a module runs. Two modules at a year each is a reading, not a citation. CAMPUS LIST DISAGREES WITH THE SCHOOL OWN: KSA names Wambugu, Thika, Nakuru, Ainabkoi and Ugenya; this catalogue holds Wambugu, Ugenya, Ainabkoi and Pap Konam. The school does not publish a per-programme fee schedule in any source reachable here, so no figure is shown - confirm the campus, the length and the fee together.

Programme named in Siaya National Polytechnic's published artisan course list (formerly Siaya Institute of Technology). The institution's published artisan minimum is given as a KCPE certificate or a KCSE mean grade of D-. A KCPE certificate is an alternative to the KCSE grade rather than an addition to it, so a learner holding an E clears the published bar and E is recorded. That is the same reading already applied at Kisumu, Eldoret, Kisii, Michuki and Bureti, whose published minimum has the identical shape. Recording the D- branch instead removed this course from the screen of the learner least likely to have another option, and left Siaya reading as blind to an E-grade learner while its own national polytechnic sat in the catalogue. Ask the registrar whether KCPE alone is accepted. KNEC modular courses are being phased out for CBET, so confirm which curriculum the current intake runs. Fee derived from the government's consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (effective May 2026). Artisan fees vary more than diploma fees and published per-institution figures conflict, so treat this as an order of magnitude and confirm with the registrar.

Taita Taveta University is public and CUE-chartered at Voi, and it is Kenya's mining university - a declared Centre of Excellence in Mining, Environmental Engineering and Resource Management, with a School of Mines and Engineering that has no real equivalent in this catalogue. Its four schools are Mines and Engineering, Business Economics and Social Sciences, Science and Informatics, and Agriculture Earth and Environmental Sciences. Listed on the university's own academic programmes listing. Entry is the national KUCCPS degree minimum of C+, the door rather than the queue; engineering carries mathematics and physics requirements above it. No per-programme price exists to quote: Kenya retired the Differentiated Unit Cost in May 2023 for the Student-Centred Funding Model, under which what a student pays is set by an assessed means band, so the fee could not be verified as a course total. See the funding note on this card for what you would be asked for.

courses.course_name: Diploma in Kenya Registered Community Health Nursing (KRCHN)
courses.institution: Clive Irvine College of Health Sciences (PCEA Chogoria)
courses.verification_note: Clive Irvine College of Health Sciences sits inside PCEA Chogoria Hospital in Tharaka-Nithi County, run by the Presbyterian Church of East Africa, and has trained nurses there since 1951 - the oldest mission-hospital school in this catalogue. It is Nursing Council of Kenya accredited and TVETA registered, takes around 300 students a year and caps this programme at 200 trainees. ENTRY IS MORE OPEN HERE THAN AT KMTC AND IT IS CORROBORATED: a KCSE mean grade of C plain with a C- in Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry or Physical Science, returned by two differently phrased searches, the second naming no grade at all. KMTC asks C+ for the same award. Placement runs through KUCCPS, so confirm the current requirement on the student portal for your cycle. DURATION IS THREE YEARS, from the college's own programme page and an independent listing - the 36 months this catalogue records across most of the estate, and the opposite reading from AIC Kijabe and Tenwek, which publish three and a half for the same award. Njia records what each institution publishes rather than choosing between them. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: the only money figure any reachable source carries is Ksh 15,500 per semester for day-scholar meals. That is a catering charge, not tuition, and writing it into the fee field would understate the course by an order of magnitude. Tuition could not be verified, so none is shown - ring the admissions office and ask for tuition separately from the meals charge.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Chuka Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.

Fee derived from the government’s consolidated annual public-TVET fee of Ksh 67,189 (inclusive of assessment fees, effective May 2026), scaled to course duration. Institutes bill per term and per-course amounts can differ — confirm with the registrar.

courses.course_name: Certificate in Information Communication Technology (CDACC Level 5)
courses.verification_note: Qualification is a TVET CDACC national curriculum at Level 5, so the same competencies and external assessment apply wherever it is taught. Entry at Level 4/5 is a KCSE mean grade of D plain — the reason this record exists, since Njia's business and finance clusters were until now almost entirely closed below C-. Institutes bill per term and per-course amounts differ — confirm with the registrar, and confirm the college is currently accredited to assess this qualification. The centre is a COUNTY vocational training centre, and vocational training is a devolved function: each county government sets the fees chargeable in its own VTCs, so the national consolidated public-TVET rate does not govern this course and the county publishes no per-course figure that could be verified. WHAT NJIA FOUND, AND COULD NOT RECONCILE: this record previously showed Ksh 67,189 derived from the national rate. That rate is set for colleges a learner is PLACED into by KUCCPS - the Ministry's May 2026 standardisation directive scopes itself to national polytechnics, technical training institutes, institutes of science and technology and vocational colleges - and a county VTC charge is far lower, so the figure over-quoted this course many times over. It is withdrawn rather than replaced by a guess. Ask the centre what it charges for this award per term, and whether the CDACC assessment fee is on top. Programme named in Ebukanga Technical and Vocational College's published artisan list as Artisan in General Fitting (KNEC), offered for a maximum of 20 trainees. The college is publicly managed under the Ministry of Education and TVETA-accredited at Diploma, Craft and Artisan levels. DURATION IS NOT PUBLISHED and is shown as absent rather than guessed. KNEC publishes no single artisan duration - one year for some awards, two years with industrial attachment for others - and the nearest published figure, one year for the Artisan Certificate in Fitting and Turning, is a DIFFERENT named award. Course identity here is (name, institution), so that figure is not transferred. Entry: the college states its artisan tier takes a KCSE mean grade of D- or below, and the KNEC artisan minimum is a KCPE certificate or equivalent - an alternative to a mean grade rather than an addition to it, so a learner holding an E clears the published bar and the tier is recorded as open entry. Fee could not be verified: the public-TVET rate of Ksh 67,189 is annual and cannot be scaled without a duration, so no figure is shown rather than a derived one resting on a guess. Ask the registrar for the length and the current fee.

courses.institution: Kenya Medical Training College (KMTC) — Vihiga Campus
courses.verification_note: KMTC publishes one national fee structure for every campus: Ksh 82,200 in Year 1 and Ksh 78,000 each subsequent year, 2025/26 (kmtc.ac.ke, August 2026). Totals here are that schedule multiplied out by course length. Tuition only — accommodation, meals and skills-lab charges are extra and vary by campus. A non-refundable Ksh 1,500 application fee applies. Confirm with the campus before paying. Entry was previously recorded here as a D+ mean grade. That was wrong, and the error is worth naming: D+ is the BIOLOGY SUBJECT requirement for this award, not the mean grade, and it had been written into the mean-grade field. KMTC publishes a minimum KCSE mean grade of C- for every certificate programme, with the cluster-subject requirement on top - for this course a D+ in Biology or Biological Sciences and a D in one of Mathematics, Chemistry, Physics or Physical Sciences. So the C- is needed overall AND the subject grades on top. The duration and the fee moved with it: the certificate runs two years rather than one, so the national schedule multiplies out to Ksh 160,200 instead of Ksh 82,200.
